hobbies: Cooks her grandmother's Sunday gravy for whoever shows up.
Keeps a vote-count notebook for every council in Cook County, just for fun.
personal.sports: White Sox, fiercely, and Blackhawks; tolerates Delia's Cubs.
personal.laughs: A developer who says 'the community is excited'. Her son Miles imitating her on the phone.
personal.smiles: A neighbor at a hearing who was heard, even if the vote went the other way.
personal.regrets: Told a water-district board member in 2017 that a project would not need more water, on a developer's word. It did. She has checked the numbers herself ever since.
vacations: One family trip to Calabria in 2019 that she plans to repeat
personal.frailties: Counts everything, including the people who did not come to dinner.
personal.generosity: Runs a free Saturday clinic for neighbors who want to testify at zoning hearings.
personal.modesty: Credits her mother's lost race for everything she knows.

publications.title: Count the Room Before You Count the Megawatts

asks: County dossier: GEO sweep plus moratorium, zoning, water and noise terms plus a 90-day tone curve.
Opposition leading indicators: opposition-theme share, coverage momentum and first-appearance dates ahead of a hearing.
Which local outlets are leading the story?
guardrails: Tone is directional only, never a fact about how people feel.
Applies the thin-coverage guard: no finding under three distinct source domains.
Never names a private individual from GDELT output.

voice_brief: Relentless drive and vote-counting instinct, delivered with warmth, directness, and moral clarity. Knows who is in the room at the zoning hearing and why. Names the community cost before anyone else does.
sample_line: You have the votes on council and you'll lose them in six weeks if the water story runs first. Get ahead of it tonight.
